Teddy’s appointment was for 3:00 p.m., and while I understand delays happen, they arrived at 4:35 p.m.—almost two hours late. Again, that should have been a warning. They took Teddy for about an hour, then told me their mobile truck’s generator had broken, so they were taking him in their mobile taxi to their brick-and-mortar store, which I thought was kind of cool. They left my house at 5:57 p.m. Time passed, and by 7:45 p.m., they still had Teddy. I started worrying—was he okay, did something happen? You know how the mind works. I texted, and they said the taxi was leaving their store and he’d be home soon. Still nothing, so I texted again at 8:30 p.m. and got no reply. Teddy finally came home at 8:41 p.m. The best part? With everything that happened, there was no apology, and I was charged full price. All I can say is my dog will never go to this mobile pet business again. Not recommended.
